    Lemma 8.8, geometric part: finitely many orbits cannot cover a large zero set #

    That paper (lem:dimension-infinity): "The representation variety is a nonempty zero set of at most F scalar polynomial equations in affine N-space; the zero arrow assignment is a point. Every component of such a zero set has dimension at least N − F. The change-of-basis group has dimension D, and its simultaneous scalar subgroup stabilizes every representation. An orbit has dimension equal to that of the group minus that of the stabilizer, so each orbit has dimension at most D − 1. The variety cannot be a finite union of these orbits."

    Setting: arrows a : s a → t a between vertices with dimensions d, representation space of matrices x_a ∈ k^{d(t a) × d(s a)}, the group ∏ GL_{d v} acting by x_a ↦ g_{t a} x_a g_{s a}⁻¹. Formalization of the dimension count:

    • (step 1) the zero set X of F polynomials vanishing at 0: dim k[x]/I ≥ N − F by Krull's height theorem at the origin, whose height is N (a chain of coordinate primes);
    • (step 2) an orbit is covered by the images of the charts g_c = 1 of the group (scalar invariance), each a localization of a polynomial ring in D − 1 variables; the vanishing ideal J_{x,c} of a chart image is prime and dim k[x]/J_{x,c} ≤ D − 1 (Noether normalization and transcendence degree);
    • (step 3) by the Nullstellensatz a prime over I contains some J_{x,c}, so dim k[x]/I ≤ D − 1.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
